title: css: fix green/blue channel swap in oklch gamut mapping
body:
`gamut_mapping_xyz_to_srgb`'s binary search calls `srgb_to_oklab(clipped_r, clipped_b, clipped_g)` when measuring how far the clipped color has drifted from the original, swapping the green and blue arguments. The very next line computes the comparison point with the correct `r, g, b` order, so the JND check ends up comparing against the wrong OKLab point and can settle on a less accurate clipped chroma.

Most existing test colors didn't catch this because they either stay in-gamut or happen to have green ≈ blue, making the swap a no-op. With channels far enough apart it's visible: `.a{color:oklch(0.65 0.3 50)}` targeting chrome90 lowers to `#de6800` instead of the correct `#e56300`.

Added two oklch cases with separated g/b to `TestColorFunctions` and fixed six stale hex values in `TestGradient` that were asserting the buggy output.
